subject: Service continuity stipend & billing reconciliation - Stardust Labs
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@stardust.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@stardust.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected multi-day latency window — request for stipend/reconciliation

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this — we had a severe latency degradation across our ingestion pipelines between Feb 1 00:00 UTC and Feb 2 14:00 UTC. Our ops team captured the requests and attached a timeline + token usage export. The incident impacted three production jobs and caused delayed deliveries to customers.

We appreciate Redwood’s rapid mitigation but the customer-facing impact is material. Can you advise whether Redwood will consider a one-time service continuity stipend (billing reconciliation) while we finalize acceptance testing after the incident?

What we’d like to see (proposal from our side):
- Proportional billing reconciliation for Feb monthly invoice window for the affected service (we calculate ~18% of affected usage)
- A short-term guarantee/escrow that ensures priority routing and a small credits pool to prevent repeated hits while we finish onboarding
- A simple MOU to formalize the scope of the stipend and the timing for bookkeeping adjustments

I’m attaching the incident_timeline.pdf and usage_report_feb.csv for reference.

Happy to hop on a quick call today if helpful.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform | Stardust Labs
elena@stardust.ai
+1 415-555-0192

---
Attachments: incident_timeline.pdf (PDF), usage_report_feb.csv (CSV)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@stardust.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Feb 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected multi-day latency window — request for stipend/reconciliation

Elena — thanks for the detail and for the timeline + usage export. I’m sorry Stardust was hit; we take availability issues seriously.

We’ll review the attachments and pull the incident log from our side. I want to be transparent about how we handle these: for standard outages we offer pro-rated credits under the SLA; for tiered commercial customers we can consider one-time stipends or goodwill vouchers where the operational impact is outsized.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) I’ll escalate to Sales Ops and Finance for a quick reconciliation estimate.
2) CS (Marissa) will validate the customer-facing impact and confirm affected resources.
3) If the numbers align, I’ll request an exec approval for a one-time service continuity stipend and suggest an escrow-style arrangement you proposed (short-lived, applied to next invoice).

Could you confirm the customer legal entity for invoicing and if procurement prefers a DocuSign MOU or a short email acceptance?

Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Feb 2028 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Stardust incident — recommended remediation package

Naomi / Jonas — quick internal note after looking at the usage export and replaying logs:
- Affected tokens ~ 2.1M across three projects during the window (matches their CSV)
- Impacted routes are on hosted inference with standard plan (not Dedicated)
- Customer is high-growth, likely to expand if we keep reliability tight.

Recommendation (to present for exec approval):
- One-time service continuity stipend equal to 20% of the affected usage (applied as an invoice credit on next billing cycle) OR a capped $14,000 goodwill voucher (whichever is higher for the customer)
- Short-term priority routing (30 days) via an automatic cap on our queuing for affected routes (no cost during the month)
- Offer a 30-day Dedicated trial at a discounted onboarding rate if they commit to a 6-month Dedicated pilot within 30 days

Attachments: stardust_mou_draft.docx (template for the MOU).

We’ll need an exec sign-off on the stipend amount and the voucher cap. If Finance wants to classify this as a billing adjustment vs. credit voucher, we should confirm now so procurement can accept the format.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

On Fri, Feb 3, 2028 at 10:05 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the detail...
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: finance-approvals@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Feb 2028 09:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Stardust incident — recommended remediation package

Naomi / Marissa / Karthik — reviewed Marissa’s recommendation. Given Stardust’s ARR profile and the impact window, I approve the following, subject to legal and finance confirmation:

- Approve one-time service continuity stipend equal to 20% of the affected usage, applied as a credit against the Feb invoice (Finance to reconcile exact USD amount)
- Approve priority routing for 30 days (ops to implement and monitor)
- Approve a capped $10k goodwill voucher alternative if finance opts for voucher classification instead of billing credit

Conditions:
1) Legal to sign a short MOU confirming scope of the stipend and that it is a one-time concession (no SLA precedent beyond this incident).
2) Finance must validate the ledger treatment and confirm whether this needs a journal entry or a voucher code.
3) We require Stardust’s procurement acknowledgement (email or DocuSign) before applying the adjustment.

Please circulate the MOU draft and finance estimate. I’ll backstop approval if there are nuanced asks from their procurement.

Jonas Weber
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai

Elena — good news. Execs have approved a one-time service continuity stipend with conditions. Below is the summary and next steps so procurement has everything in one place: 

Summary of approved package: 
- One-time credit equal to 20% of affected usage (Finance will confirm USD amount; expected ~$15,600 based on their CSV) applied against the Feb invoice OR a capped $10,000 goodwill voucher if Stardust prefers a voucher code
- 30 days of priority routing (no additional charge) starting upon MOU acceptance
- Optional: 30-day Dedicated trial onboarding discount if Stardust signs a 6-month pilot within 30 days

Action items and timeline: 
1) We’ve attached a draft MOU for quick review (stardust_mou_draft.docx). Please confirm procurement preference: DocuSign or email acceptance.
2) Finance will produce the final credit amount and the ledger treatment by EOD Tue, Feb 14. finance-approvals@redwood.ai is on copy.
3) Once MOU acceptance is received, ops will enable the priority routing within 24 hours.

Please reply with: 1) acceptance method, 2) preferred remedy (invoice credit vs voucher), and 3) billing entity name for paperwork.

Thanks for collaborating on this — we want to make sure your customers see the service continuity.

Best,
